item.title: On the Topology of the Set of Nonnegative Forms That Are Not Sums of Squares
item.description: arXiv:2611.07252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the topology of the normalized space of real nonnegative forms of degree $2d$ in $n$ variables that are not sums of squares. Whenever it is nonempty, we prove that it is path-connected but not acyclic, and in particular not contractible. We give explicit bounds on the degrees in which its reduced homology can be nonzero. In the two minimal nonempty cases, we show an embedding of an exterior algebra into the cohomology ring, and prove containment of the binary octahedral and binary icosahedral groups, respectively, in its fundamental group.
item.dc:creator: Maximilian Illmer, Tim Netzer

item.title: On bordism classes of symmetric products of surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.07813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explicitly determine the complex bordism class of the $n$-th symmetric product of a complex curve of genus $g$. In particular, we provide an explicit formula expressing this class as an integral linear combination of bordism classes of products of complex projective spaces. Similarly, we determine the unoriented bordism class of the $n$-th symmetric product of a non-orientable surface of genus $g$ (i.e., $\#_{i=1}^{g+1}\mathbb R P^2$). It turns out that these classes are also expressed as a $\mathbb Z_2$-linear combination of bordism classes of products of even-dimensional real projective spaces. We also give an affirmative answer to a non-orientable version of the Blagojevi\'c--Gruji\'c--\v{Z}ivaljevi\'c conjecture stating that the topological type of any symmetric product of a noncompact surface of finite type determines the topological type of the surface itself.
item.dc:creator: Georgy Chernykh, Dmitry Gugnin

item.title: Topological classification of Bazaikin spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.07898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish a topological classification of Bazaikin spaces whose sixth cohomology groups have orders prime to \(5\). Moreover, we obtain an estimate for the number of diffeomorphism types among these spaces.
item.dc:creator: Fuquan Fang, Wen Shen

item.title: A Story of Algebra and Categories I: Algebraic Theories
item.description: arXiv:2611.07927v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This is the first part of a series of expository notes on homotopical and categorical algebra. It charts a course from ordinary algebraic structures such as monoids, groups, and rings to their various homotopy-coherent generalizations and equivariant versions. The emphasis is on the ideas that lead to and connect the constructions, as well as where and how they appear in nature.
item.dc:creator: Lior Yanovski

item.title: Exotic smooth structures on complex projective spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.08406v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study smooth structures on the topological manifold underlying complex projective space. We conjecture that every complex projective space $\mathbb{CP}^n$ with $n>3$ admits an exotic smooth structure. We prove two results providing strong evidence for this conjecture. First, the set of complex dimensions $n$ for which $\mathbb{CP}^n$ admits an exotic smooth structure has natural density one. Second, we explicitly identify $266$ congruence classes modulo $288$ such that $\mathbb{CP}^n$ admits an exotic smooth structure whenever $n>3$ lies in one of these classes. These classes cover more than $92\%$ of complex dimensions, improving the previously known lower bound of approximately $36\%$. We prove these results by first relating the concordance group of $\mathbb{CP}^n$ to suitable Atiyah--Hirzebruch filtration subgroups of its stable cohomotopy group, and then applying computations in chromatic homotopy theory at height $2$.
item.dc:creator: Yueshi Hou, Hana Jia Kong, Zhouli Xu

item.title: Braided Multisections and Akhmedov's Fake Quadrics
item.description: arXiv:2611.06949v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give handlebody decompositions of the complements of the cyclic multisections in $\Sigma_g\times S^2$ constructed in~\cite{AB}. The 2-handle framings are induced by the product coordinates. We compute the integral homology of the complements from their handle chain complexes, including the torsion subgroup of $H_2$. For the degree pairs $(3,3)$ and $(2,4)$, we specify surface diffeomorphisms inducing the maps on first homology prescribed in~\cite{AY} and recover the integral first homology groups $(\Z/3)^2\oplus\Z/(3m)$ and $(\Z/2)^2\oplus\Z/(4m)$, respectively, for $m\geq1$. For the symmetric $m=1$ sum, we also give a simultaneous surface diagram of the relative product attachments and identify their product framings with the surface framings. The resulting symplectic sums are aspherical and symplectically minimal, and have the rational cohomology ring of $S^2\times S^2$.
item.dc:creator: Anar Akhmedov

item.title: ToroFit: Fitting Wedge Sums of Tori to High-Dimensional Data
item.description: arXiv:2611.06990v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Data arising in scientific applications often exhibits complex nonlinear structure. Identifying and parameterizing said nonlinearities can enable better modeling, enhance predictive analysis, data interpolation, denoising, and anomaly detection. In this paper, we develop theoretical and computational methods to detect and parametrize Euclidean point cloud data lying near a wedge sum of tori. Specifically, we use persistent cohomology and cup products to identify the distinct toroidal components, and on each component, we optimize over low-energy multivariate trigonometric polynomials for best data fit. The ensuing optimization problem reduces to generalized ridge regression, which can be solved efficiently via standard techniques. We demonstrate the utility of the proposed framework in both synthetic and real datasets, including interpolation of low frame-rate recurrent videos, attractor recovery in quasiperiodic dynamical systems, and the parametrization of gene-space cycle data for parasites and humans.
item.dc:creator: Tanishq Bhatia, Jose A. Perea, Tarek M. Zikry

item.title: Multipartite Entanglement, TQFT Partition Functions and PL Bordism
item.description: arXiv:2611.07000v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In a previous work we conjectured that the multi-invariants of the ground state of a gapped $(d-1)+1$-dimensional system, labeled by bipartite $(d+1)$-edge-colored graphs encoding closed oriented $d$-manifolds $M$, compute the partition functions $Z(M)$ of the low energy topological quantum field theory (TQFT), up to non-universal factors determined by the local structure of the triangulation. In this paper we determine which combinations of partition functions can be isolated from the non-universal factors. The answer is governed by oriented bordism. If $M$ is null-bordant, $Z(M)$ is obtained from an explicit, state-independent finite family of multi-invariants, up to a power of $Z(S^d)$ which is fixed to be $Z(S^d)^{\chi(M)/2}$ for even $d$ and can be removed for odd $d$. Conversely, the obstruction is measured by a quotient of the group of "residues" of colored graphs which receives a surjective map from the oriented bordism group, with kernel precisely the torsion subgroup as far as smooth manifolds are concerned. In $d=4$ the obstruction is the signature: $Z(M)/Z(S^4)^{\chi(M)/2}$ can be extracted if and only if $\sigma(M)=0$. This is due to the fact that the first Pontryagin class $p_1$ has a local expression and thus $e^{i\theta\sigma(M)}=e^{\frac{i}{3}\theta\int_M p_1}$ cannot be separated from the non-universal factors. Torsion invariants, in contrast, are not obstructed: for the ground state of the $4+1$-dimensional invertible phase with partition function $(-1)^{\int w_2w_3}$ we compute the multi-invariants exactly, and two graphs with identical local data, encoding the Dold manifold and $\mathbb{CP}^2\times S^1$, give opposite signs.
item.dc:creator: Michele Del Zotto, Abhijit Gadde, Pavel Putrov

item.title: Higher Noncommutative Motives and Higher K-theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.07262v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct higher additive noncommutative motives of stable $(\infty,n)$-categories, extending the additive motives of Blumberg, Gepner, and Tabuada and the secondary theory of Mazel-Gee and Stern. We formulate a notion of exact sequences and establish the universal property of the resulting additive motives. We give two equivalent constructions: a localization of enriched presheaves and a weighted Waldhausen $S$-construction on complete exact flags. We then compute their Hom objects, obtaining ordinary K-theory at the first level and lower additive motives recursively at higher levels. Our results recover the classical and secondary theories, provide coherent multiplicative structures, and yield an endofunctor on the category of Stefanich rings. In short, higher motives are higher K-theory.
item.dc:creator: Hisato Matsukawa

item.title: The universal property of the decomposition space of quasisymmetric functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.08063v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Aguiar, Bergeron, and Sottile showed that the coalgebra of quasisymmetric functions is terminal among connected graded coalgebras with a zeta function. After developing the notions of gradings and zeta functions for decomposition spaces, we establish an objective homotopic version of this result. Namely, the decomposition space $Q$ of quasisymmetric functions is terminal: for any conservatively graded decomposition space $X$ with zeta function $F$, there is a unique graded ikeo-culf span $X \leftarrow W \rightarrow Q$ inducing $F$ from the special zeta function on $Q$. More generally, for gradings in any complete decomposition space $M$ with indecomposable identities, the terminal object is $J(M)$, the free decomposition space on the nondegenerate simplices of $M$; the quasisymmetric case is $Q=J(B\mathbb{N})$.
item.dc:creator: Philip Hackney, Joachim Kock, Jan Steinebrunner

item.title: Shades and Convexity of Hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.08415v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $f\colon M^n\to\mathbf{R}^{n+1}$, $n\geq2$, be a smooth immersion of a closed oriented manifold, with Gauss map $\nu\colon M\to\mathbf{S}^n$. For each unit vector $u$, the shade $S_u\subset M$ is the set of points where $\nu$ makes an acute angle with $u$. We show that $f$ is a convex embedding if and only if every shade is contractible. More generally, if every shade is $k$-connected, then $f$ is a convex embedding provided that $n\leq 2k+1$, or $n=2k+2$ and $H_{k+1}(M;\mathbf{Z})=0$. On the other hand, for every $n\geq 2k+3$ there is a nonconvex embedding $f\colon\mathbf{S}^n\to\mathbf{R}^{n+1}$ all of whose shades are $k$-connected. These results give sharp answers to a question of H. Wente in all dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Ghomi

item.title: Higher path groupoids and the holonomy of formal power series connections
item.description: arXiv:2506.23880v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Building on ideas of Kohno, we develop a framework for the construction of higher holonomy functors via the transport of formal power series connections. Using these techniques, we obtain functors from the path groupoid, the path 2-groupoid, and the path 3-groupoid of a manifold. We show that the resulting higher holonomy functors can detect non-trivial classes in higher homotopy groups. As an application, we construct a Gray functor from the path 3-groupoid of the configuration space of $m$ points in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $n\geqslant 4$ and compute its restriction to 3-tracks with constant boundary when $n=4$.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Cellot

item.title: Morse flow categories as exit path categories
item.description: arXiv:2605.27112v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the topological flow category $\mathcal{M}$ arising from a Morse-Smale pair $(f,\xi)$ on a smooth closed manifold $X$ is equivalent, as an $\infty$-category, to Lurie's $\infty$-category $\mathrm{Sing}_A(X)$ of exit paths in $X$ with respect to the stratification by the stable manifolds of $\xi$. The objects of $\mathcal{M}$ are the critical points of $f$, and for every pair of critical points, the space of morphisms of $\mathcal{M}$ between these is the space of possibly broken trajectories of $\xi$ connecting them; it can be identified up to homotopy with the space of unbroken ones. The latter maps naturally to the space of exit paths connecting these critical points; we prove this map to be a weak homotopy equivalence. Then, we combine these ingredients with several others to construct a zigzag of equivalences between the homotopy coherent nerve of $\mathcal{M}$, denoted $\mathcal{N}(\mathcal{M})$, and $\mathrm{Sing}_A(X)$. The $n$-simplices of $\mathcal{N}(\mathcal{M})$ are homotopy coherent diagrams of $n$ composable morphisms of $\mathcal{M}$; we introduce the notion of unbroken diagram, yielding an $\infty$-subcategory of $\mathcal{N}(\mathcal{M})$, which we refer to as the flow coherent nerve of $\mathcal{M}$. The simplices of the latter give rise to stratified maps out of a family of stratified cubes, into $X$. We organize this family into a functor from the category of finite ordered sequences of critical points, to the category of $A$-stratified topological spaces, and we prove a comparison result with the usual stratified geometric realization functor. We finally use a theorem of Tanaka that associates a functor to a semi-simplicial map between $\infty$-categories that satisfies certain conditions. Our theorem has implications regarding constructible sheaves and the description of homotopy types in terms of flow categories.
item.dc:creator: Colin Fourel

item.title: Multicomplexes in Action: Strong Formality of Compact Hyperk\"ahler Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.40639v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that all compact hyperk\"ahler manifolds are bigraded strongly formal in the sense of Milivojevi\'c and Stelzig, proving that in the context of pluripotential homotopy theory they play the same role as compact K\"ahler manifolds in rational homotopy theory. Indeed, the main result arises from general algebraic considerations on categories of objects with more differentials, that of $n$-complexes and commutative $n$-differential graded algebras. For them we discuss a standard model category structure, introduce a generalization of the $\partial\bar{\partial}$-Lemma and establish an algebraic formality theorem.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Pio Contr\`o

item.title: A Topological Formula for Potts Lattice Gauge Theory Correlations
item.description: arXiv:2607.02434v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We exhibit a formula relating the correlation between Wilson loop variables in Potts lattice gauge theory to a topological quantity in the plaquette random cluster model. As applications we prove exponential decay of correlations between slowly growing Wilson loop variables for Ising lattice gauge theory on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ at all but the critical temperature, we demonstrate that the correlation length is finite at sufficiently high or low temperatures in any dimension, and we show that the correlation length of the model on $\mathbb{Z}^4$ with free boundary conditions equals that of the dual model with constant boundary conditions when $q$ is prime.
item.dc:creator: Paul Duncan, Benjamin Schweinhart

item.title: Anti-successors and anti-replicators, Manin products and Koszul duality
item.description: arXiv:2610.21365v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop an operadic theory of anti-splitting and anti-replicating for binary operads. For a binary operad $\opd$, we define its anti-bisuccessor $\ABSu(\opd)$ and anti-trisuccessor $\ATSu(\opd)$. Each generating operation is recovered as the negative sum of two or three split operations, yielding canonical operad morphisms $\opd\to\ABSu(\opd)$ and $\opd\to\ATSu(\opd)$. For binary quadratic operads, these constructions are described by Manin black products: \[ \ABSu(\opd)\cong\antiprelie\bullet\opd, \qquad \ATSu(\opd)\cong\antipostlie\bullet\opd. \] Dually, we also introduce the canonical quadratic anti-duplicator and anti-triplicator, together with their combinatorial counterparts defined by labeled planar binary trees. We show that they coincide precisely under a full-support condition. As applications, we obtain anti-dupli-com and anti-dupli-Lie algebras. We also display an example in which the two constructions differ. Furthermore, we establish the Koszul duality relations \[ \widehat{\ADup}(\opd^!) \cong\ABSu(\opd)^!, \qquad \widehat{\ATrip}(\opd^!) \cong\ATSu(\opd)^!, \] providing an effective description of the canonical quadratic anti-duplicator in terms of the Manin white product. The framework recovers known constructions, including anti-dendriform, anti-pre-Lie and anti-pre-Poisson algebras, and produces further examples and Koszul dual pairs.
item.dc:creator: Chengming Bai, Li Guo, Yunhe Sheng, You Wang
